thread:
rachel: quick Q

We're reworking form errors for the new dashboard: inline per-field errors vs a top summary banner. thoughts?
devin: inline for most cases. users scan near field. summary banner useful for submission-level failures (eg. cross-field or permissions)
theo: agree. inline for 1:1 field validation. but add a compact summary anchorable at top when there are >2 errors so mobile users notice
priya_a11y: accessibility rules: 1) announce error count with role=alert 2) focus should move to first invalid field on submit 3) summary links must focus the corresponding input (use element.focus())
nina_pm: product nuance: some teams want a single-line generic error ("check fields") for quick flows. does that conflict with accessibility needs?
rachel: generic text ok for low-friction flows, but still must highlight fields. generic-only is risky
devin: implementation note: use aria-invalid on inputs and aria-describedby pointing to the error message id. that lets SRs read field-specific messages even if summary exists
theo: UX pattern: inline message below field, 1-line. if message >2 lines or has actions (link to docs), show it in banner as well and provide anchor
priya_a11y: also avoid color-only signals. include icons/text and ensure 3:1 contrast for icons at smallest size. for required fields, prefer programmatic aria-required + visible label text on focus
nina_pm: delete confirmation question: modal currently says "Delete workspace" with checkbox "I know this is permanent". should we force typed confirm for workspaces with >5 repos?
devin: risk-tiering again. typed confirm for high-risk items, checkbox+undo for small ones. also show list of linked resources in modal for context
priya_a11y: typed confirm needs aria-live for mismatch and explicit instructions. set autocomplete off. ensure screen readers don't repeat label and input redundantly
rachel: next steps: implement inline-first pattern, top summary when errors exceed 2 or are cross-field, accessibility checklist (aria-invalid, aria-describedby, role=alert, focus-first-invalid), and risk-tiered typed confirm for big deletes. i'll make mocks and an acceptance checklist and post back
